items.name: Trout
items.description: Fresh trout from Crownmere. Cook it over a range or campfire.

items.name: Cooked Trout
items.description: Trout cooked through over the fire.

items.name: Burnt Trout
items.description: Charred through and inedible.

items.name: Tuna
items.description: Fresh tuna from Crownmere. Cook it over a range or campfire.

items.name: Cooked Tuna
items.description: Tuna cooked through over the fire.

items.name: Burnt Tuna
items.description: Charred through and inedible.

items.name: Salmon
items.description: Fresh salmon from Pearlwater. Cook it over a range or campfire.

items.name: Cooked Salmon
items.description: Salmon cooked through over the fire.

items.name: Burnt Salmon
items.description: Charred through and inedible.

items.name: Gold
items.description: Plain gold coins. Every shop and settlement takes them.

items.name: Copper Ore
items.description: Grey ore, streaked rust-red. Smelts easily, which is the only nice thing about it.

items.name: Limestone
items.description: Crumbly limestone from the Copper Pit. Every furnace on the frontier runs on it as flux.

items.name: Iron Ore
items.description: Dark deepwood ore. Heavier than it looks and slightly oily on the break.

items.name: Cobalt Ore
items.description: Black Highlands ore with a blue fracture. It takes a furnace twice to give anything up.

items.name: Titanium Ore
items.description: Rust-orange Ashlands ore, warm off the seam. It smells faintly of a banked fire.

items.name: Flux Stone
items.description: Grey-black flux off the Quarry Seams. Titanium refuses to run without it.

items.name: Pine Log
items.description: Pale, straight-grained, and dries in a day. The march is short of everything except this.

items.name: Ash Log
items.description: Close-grained ash from the Woodlands canopy. Seasoned for strong handles and shields.

items.name: Oak Log
items.description: Dense oak with a coarse, durable grain. It holds a Cobalt ferrule without splitting.

items.name: Walnut Log
items.description: Dark walnut heartwood from broad, spreading crowns. It cuts cleanly and takes a smooth finish.

items.name: Minnow
items.description: A palm-sized fish out of the River shallows. Raw, it is mostly bone.

items.name: Trout
items.description: Black-backed trout from the Blackwater pools. Fights the line the whole way in.

items.name: Perch
items.description: A slab-sided tarn fish with a spined dorsal. Hillcrest eats little else.

items.name: Bass
items.description: A dark-finned spring fish that thrives where the water runs warm. Oily and rich.

items.name: Copper Bar
items.description: One ore, one stone, one bar. The first thing anybody makes.

items.name: Iron Bar
items.description: Dark and dense. Rings a full tone lower than Copper on the anvil.

items.name: Cobalt Bar
items.description: Black with a blue sheen. Holds an edge through cairn stone, which is why Hillcrest exists.

items.name: Titanium Bar
items.description: Three ores and two flux stones a bar, and it comes off the furnace still glowing at the core.

items.name: Quartz
items.description: A milky chip out of a Copper seam. Holds a charge just long enough to be useful.

items.name: Amber
items.description: Fossil resin from under the deepwood. Warm in the hand and nobody knows why.

items.name: Garnet
items.description: Deep red, cut square by the rock itself. Hillcrest jewellers cage it in Cobalt.

items.name: Fire Opal
items.description: An orange stone with a live spark in it. Ashford cages them in Titanium claws.

items.name: Pine Shaft
items.description: A shaved length of pine. Handle, haft, or half a staff.

items.name: Ash Shaft
items.description: Ash, turned down and oiled. Will not warp in Woodlands damp.

items.name: Oak Shaft
items.description: Resinous, springy, and heavy. Takes a Cobalt ferrule without splitting.

items.name: Walnut Shaft
items.description: A straight walnut shaft, shaped and seasoned for rods and staves.

items.name: Pine Handle
items.description: A short pine grip, shaped for a Copper tang or tool head.

items.name: Ash Handle
items.description: Oiled ash with enough weight to balance an Iron head.

items.name: Oak Handle
items.description: Oak shaped around the grain so a Cobalt tang will not split it.

items.name: Walnut Handle
items.description: An oiled walnut grip shaped to hold a Titanium tang securely.

items.name: Coarse Hide
items.description: Goat and rabbit skins, scraped and salted together. Stiff until you work it.

items.name: Thick Hide
items.description: Deepwood deer and hog, thorns still in the seam. Nothing in Woodlands tans clean.

items.name: Fur Pelt
items.description: Winter coat off something that lived above the treeline. Takes no dye and does not tear.

items.name: Heavy Hide
items.description: Foothill hide seared grey at the edges. Sheds heat the way fur pelt sheds cold.

items.name: Air Essence
items.description: A stackable charge drawn from the distant Farmland cache.

items.name: Earth Essence
items.description: Dense green-brown essence mined beneath the Woodlands roots.

items.name: Water Essence
items.description: Cold blue essence gathered from the far Highlands cache.

items.name: Fire Essence
items.description: A hot orange charge mined at the Ashlands altar ruins. It never quite cools.

items.name: Mind Rune
items.description: A pale rune etched with a single clear eye. It steadies the caster's thought onto one mark. Rank-one invocations spend one per cast.

items.name: Chaos Rune
items.description: An orange rune scored with a jagged fork. It lets a spell break loose and scatter across a line of foes. Rank-two invocations spend one per cast.

items.name: Death Rune
items.description: A bone-white rune cut with a hollow skull. It holds a spell's shape while it gathers and closes. Rank-three invocations spend one per cast.

items.name: Blood Rune
items.description: A dark red rune with a drop sunk into its face. It feeds invocations heavy enough to batter the ground. Rank-four invocations spend one per cast.

items.name: Wrath Rune
items.description: A black rune split through with slow red light. The four finales spend one per cast, and nothing smaller touches it.

items.name: Cosmic Rune
items.description: A yellow rune ringed with a wheel of stars. It spreads an invocation across an area. Every area invocation spends one beside its rank rune.

items.name: Hen Feather
items.description: Barred brown, still stiff at the quill. Fletchers buy them by the double handful.

items.name: Hen Egg
items.description: Warm when you find it, which is how you know you were quick enough.

items.name: Curled Horn
items.description: One horn from a goat. Hollow, and loud if you know how to blow it.

items.name: Ox Horn
items.description: Short, thick and scarred at the base. Millfield turns them into cups and lamp horn.

items.name: Rabbit Foot
items.description: Carried for luck by everyone who has ever admitted the moor frightens them.

items.name: Marsh Gland
items.description: Pale sac from behind a frog's jaw. Keeps essence wet, which is most of the trick.

items.name: Viper Skin
items.description: Shed whole and inside out. Copper fletchers back their nocks with it.

items.name: Venom Gland
items.description: Still full. Handled with the same care you would give a lit lamp in a barn.

items.name: Stag Antler
items.description: A six-point stag antler. Cut and polished, it makes a strong knife handle.

items.name: Curved Tusk
items.description: Ivory, yellowed, and ground to an edge by the animal's own jaw.

items.name: Wolf Fang
items.description: Long in the root, which is the part nobody expects until they pull one.

items.name: Bear Claw
items.description: Longer than a finger and blunt from stone. Hillcrest hangs them over doorways.

items.name: Boar Bristle
items.description: A fistful of black wire off a wild boar's shoulder. It will not lie flat.

items.name: Ibex Horn
items.description: Ridged the whole length, one ring a winter. This one counted eleven.

items.name: Aurochs Horn
items.description: As long as your arm and heavier. The terrace herds are the last ones anywhere.

items.name: Rat Tail
items.description: Stone Cavern pays a bounty per tail. Nobody in Hillcrest asks what the count is for.

items.name: Scorpion Stinger
items.description: Barb and bulb both intact. Dry, it is a needle; wet, it is still a problem.

items.name: Crab Claw
items.description: Off a giant crab, and big enough to have taken a pick handle in half.

items.name: Dire Bear Claw
items.description: Grey to the root, like the bear it came off. Ashford doors hang two, crossed.

items.name: Dire Boar Tusk
items.description: A boar tusk stained kiln-black. The point still goes through boot leather.

items.name: Large Ibex Horn
items.description: Ridged ibex horn with a red cast the foothill dust never washes out of.

items.name: Giant Viper Fang
items.description: An viper fang the colour of cooling slag. Hot to the touch for a day after the kill.

items.name: Raw Game Meat
items.description: Whatever the Farmland was carrying. Fowl, goat or rabbit, jointed the same way.

items.name: Roast Game
items.description: Turned over a range until the fat stops running. Frontier cooking, and it works.

items.name: Burnt Game
items.description: Left on the range. Black through and nothing left worth eating.

items.name: Raw Venison
items.description: Dark, close-grained deepwood meat. Hangs two days before it is worth cooking.

items.name: Roast Venison
items.description: Seared hard and rested. The one meal in Oakwood nobody complains about.

items.name: Burnt Venison
items.description: A stag walked all summer for this and you left it on the coals.

items.name: Raw Haunch
items.description: A whole hind quarter off something that lived above the treeline. Heavy.

items.name: Roast Haunch
items.description: Four hours over Hillcrest coals. It is a meal and most of a day's carrying.

items.name: Burnt Haunch
items.description: Ruined, and it was the biggest thing you killed all week.

items.name: Raw Prime Haunch
items.description: A hind quarter off a foothill beast, marbled from a life spent on warm ground.

items.name: Roast Prime Haunch
items.description: Cooked slow over walnut coals. Ashford calls it a wage, not a meal.

items.name: Burnt Prime Haunch
items.description: The one place in Ashlands where more fire was not the answer.

items.name: Seared Minnow
items.description: Two minutes over a range and it stops being mostly bone.

items.name: Burnt Minnow
items.description: Charred through. Nothing left worth eating.

items.name: Seared Trout
items.description: Split, salted, and laid on the stone. Oakwood's entire cuisine.

items.name: Burnt Trout
items.description: You left it on. It happens until Cooking 20.

items.name: Seared Perch
items.description: The reason anyone survives Quarry Warden's floor. Hillcrest will not sell you fewer than five.

items.name: Burnt Perch
items.description: Ninety-six gold of fish, ruined. Hillcrest has opinions about this.

items.name: Seared Bass
items.description: The oil crisps its own skin. What a Fire Ogre attempt is provisioned with.

items.name: Burnt Bass
items.description: It cooked itself the rest of the way while you watched.

items.name: Worn Pickaxe
items.description: The head is loose and the haft is somebody's fence post. One effective Mining level.

items.name: Worn Hatchet
items.description: More wedge than edge. It will get through pine if you are patient.

items.name: Worn Rod
items.description: A green stick and a length of gut. One effective Fishing level, on a good day.

items.name: Copper Pickaxe
items.description: A bar of Copper on an pine haft. Adds two effective Mining levels.

items.name: Iron Pickaxe
items.description: Iron head, ash haft. Five effective Mining levels.

items.name: Cobalt Pickaxe
items.description: Cobalt on oak. Nine effective Mining levels, and it will outlive you.

items.name: Copper Hatchet
items.description: Light, blunt-ish, and enough for pine. Two effective Woodcutting levels.

items.name: Iron Hatchet
items.description: Iron bit, deep bevel. Five effective Woodcutting levels.

items.name: Cobalt Hatchet
items.description: Goes through oak resin without gumming. Nine effective Woodcutting levels.

items.name: Pine Rod
items.description: A shaft, a hide line, and a bent pin. Two effective Fishing levels.

items.name: Ash Rod
items.description: Springy enough for a trout. Five effective Fishing levels.

items.name: Oak Rod
items.description: Built for perch, which fight like something with a grudge. Nine effective Fishing levels.

items.name: Titanium Pickaxe
items.description: An Titanium head on walnut. Seventeen effective Mining levels.

items.name: Titanium Hatchet
items.description: Bites through scorched bark without a second swing. Seventeen effective Woodcutting levels.

items.name: Walnut Rod
items.description: A flexible walnut rod built for heavy bass. Seventeen effective Fishing levels.

items.name: Willow Log
items.description: Timber cut from a willow tree.

items.name: Maple Log
items.description: Timber cut from a maple tree.

items.name: Teak Log
items.description: Timber cut from a teak tree.

items.name: Yew Log
items.description: Timber cut from a yew tree.

items.name: Magic Log
items.description: Timber cut from a magic tree.

items.description: A region-boss core used to craft a charged Air wand or staff.

items.description: A region-boss core used to craft a charged Earth wand or staff.

items.description: A ring set with cairn garnet. Grants only melee accuracy.

items.name: Cobalt Garnet Earring
items.description: A earring set with cairn garnet. Grants only melee accuracy.

items.name: Titanium Opal Ring

items.description: A earring set with fire opal. Grants only magic accuracy.

items.description: A earring set with pale quartz. Grants only defence.

items.description: A ring set with vell amber. Grants only health.

items.description: A earring set with vell amber. Grants only health.

items.description: A ring set with cairn garnet. Grants only melee power.

items.name: Cindersteel Garnet Earring
items.description: A earring set with cairn garnet. Grants only melee power.

items.name: Cindersteel Opal Ring
items.description: A ring set with fire opal. Grants only magic power.

items.name: Cindersteel Opal Earring
items.description: A earring set with fire opal. Grants only magic power.

items.name: Nightglass Opal Ring
items.description: A ring set with fire opal. Grants only vitality, critical hit chance.

items.name: Nightglass Opal Earring
items.description: A earring set with fire opal. Grants only vitality, critical hit chance.

items.name: Worn Shortsword
items.description: Notched, re-hafted twice, and lighter than it looks. It was somebody else's first.

items.name: Basic Wooden Wand
items.description: Plain brown wood from grip to socket, with no light or elemental charge.

items.name: Basic Wooden Staff
items.description: A plain two-handed staff with an empty brown socket and no glow of its own.

items.name: Worn Helm
items.description: A dented cap off somebody's scrap pile. It rattles, and it is better than bare.

items.name: Worn Cuirass
items.description: Two salvaged plates laced over old leather. The only piece of this kit that stops anything.

items.name: Worn Greaves
items.description: Mismatched shin plates tied on with cord.

items.name: Worn Gloves
items.description: Cracked leather gloves with the stitching gone at one thumb.

items.name: Worn Boots
items.description: Split-soled boots. They keep the stones out, mostly.

items.name: Worn Hide Hood
items.description: A hood cut from a hide nobody wanted. It still smells of the shed.

items.name: Worn Hide Robe
items.description: Offcuts stitched into a robe. The only piece here with enough hide to turn a claw.

items.name: Worn Hide Leggings
items.description: Hide leggings, patched at both knees.

items.name: Worn Hide Wraps
items.description: Hide strips wound over the knuckles. They keep the grip dry.

items.name: Worn Hide Boots
items.description: Soft hide boots gone thin at the heel.

items.name: Air Wand
items.description: Pine Wand fitted with a Air Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Air Staff
items.description: Pine Staff fitted with a Air Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Earth Wand
items.description: Ash Wand fitted with a Earth Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Earth Staff
items.description: Ash Staff fitted with a Earth Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Water Wand
items.description: Oak Wand fitted with a Water Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Water Staff
items.description: Oak Staff fitted with a Water Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Fire Wand
items.description: Walnut Wand fitted with a Fire Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Fire Staff
items.description: Walnut Staff fitted with a Fire Orb. Its charge pays for matching spells before carried Essence.

items.name: Fox Fur
items.description: Coarse red hair from a fox's back. Bind it around a Copper band for a padded guard ring.

items.name: Lynx Sinew
items.description: Springy tendon, cleaned and dried. A tight winding gives a hunter's ring its grip.

items.name: Badger Bristle
items.description: Stiff black and silver bristles. Worked into leg linings, they save a sheet of hide.

items.name: Porcupine Quill
items.description: A thick hollow quill with a hard point. Short sections can be set around a guard ring.

items.name: Horsehair
items.description: Long strong strands. Braided into fishing line, they replace a rod's hide binding.

items.name: Bighorn Wool
items.description: Dense wool from a ridge ram. A felted lining stretches a pelt into a pair of leggings.

items.name: Moose Antler
items.description: A flat antler section. Cut and polished, it makes a broad protective charm.

items.name: Tapir Leather
items.description: Thick strips from a tapir's flank. Trim three strips into two standard hide sheets.

items.name: Crocodile Armor Plate
items.description: A hard plate from a crocodile's back. Scute soles let one pelt cover two pairs of boots.

items.name: Salamander Secretion
items.description: A heat-stable mineral paste. Ashford uses it instead of mined flux stone.

items.name: Tortoise Shell Plate
items.description: A curved shell section. Lash several across a wooden shield in place of its metal boss.

items.name: Monitor Lizard Sinew
items.description: Heat-tough tendon from a monitor's tail. Twisted into line, it binds a Cedar rod.

items.name: Goose Down
items.description: Soft breast feathers. Pack them between hide panels to finish a robe with less leather.

items.name: Heron Quill
items.description: A long hollow flight quill. Cut around an amber bead, it steadies a casting charm.

items.name: Bustard Plume
items.description: A broad feather from a heavy moorland bird. Layered plumes replace a robe's inner pelt.

items.name: Turkey Tail Feather
items.description: A barred tail feather. Millfield hunters bind a fan of them around a small warding charm.

items.name: Snail Mucus
items.description: A sealed dab of clear adhesive. It bonds a wooden shield's layers in place of a metal boss.

items.name: Beetle Jaw
items.description: A hooked jaw hard enough to score stone. Several brace a pick head with less metal.

items.name: Centipede Chitin
items.description: Dark overlapping plates. Small segments fit an armored ring without spoiling its grip.

items.name: Spider Silk
items.description: A reel of strong dry silk. Close stitching makes a full robe from fewer hide panels.

items.name: Demon Claw
items.description: A hooked black claw. Cut down, it replaces the wooden grip beneath a Titanium blade.

items.name: Armored Dragon Scale
items.description: A broad scale with a tough leather backing. Trim several into standard heavy hide sheets.

items.name: Mantis Claw
items.description: A curved cutting spur. Its sharpened edge can be caged inside an aggressive hunting charm.

items.name: Pale Dragon Plate
items.description: A ridged shoulder plate. Riveted over a helm, it replaces part of the Cobalt shell.

items.name: Cindervein Ore
items.description: Black ore shot through with copper-red seams. Smelt three with a Molten Heart into Cindersteel.

items.name: Nightglass Ore
items.description: Violet ore with a blue fracture. Smelt three with an Astral Core into a Nightglass Bar.

items.name: Cindersteel Bar
items.description: Dense dark steel cast with a molten stone heart. Used for level 50 armour, weapons and tools.

items.name: Nightglass Bar
items.description: A solid bar of blue-black glass metal. Used for level 70 armour, weapons and tools.

items.name: Molten Heart
items.description: A cooled kernel from a living stone creature. It replaces flux when smelting Cindersteel.

items.name: Dragonhide
items.description: Supple hide beneath a young dragon's scales. Grave Thread binds it into level 50 casting armour.

items.name: Grave Thread
items.description: Black binding drawn from the Wilderness dead. Stitch Dragonhide or wind it into a Teak casting weapon.

items.name: Astral Core
items.description: A blue-violet heart from a deep Wilderness creature. It fuses Nightglass Ore without shattering it.

items.name: Starhide
items.description: Adult dragon hide steeped in deep magic. Void Thread stitches it into level 70 casting armour.

items.name: Void Thread
items.description: A dark strand pulled from a deep spirit. Binds Starhide and the crowns of Magic casting weapons.

items.name: Teak Handle
items.description: Oiled teak cut for a Cindersteel sword, pickaxe or hatchet.

items.name: Magic Handle
items.description: A carved magic-wood grip for Nightglass weapons and gathering tools.

items.name: Ashseal Iron
items.description: The Ashseal Warden's dense shield iron. Rivet it across a Teak Shield to make an Ashseal Guard.

items.name: Furnace Crown
items.description: A piece of the Furnace Regent's crucible crown. Set three around a Teak Staff to make a Regent Staff.

items.name: Chainbound Link
items.description: A living link carried by the foundry guard and Chainbound Archon. Three bind a Nightglass Sword into a Chainbound Sword.

items.name: Nightforge Seal
items.description: A breastplate stamp taken from the bastion guard or Nightforge Marshal. Reinforces Nightglass Plate into Nightmarshal Plate.

items.name: Hollow Star Fragment
items.description: A heavy black shard carried by the sanctum guard and Hollow Star. Three form the crown of a Hollowstar Staff.

items.name: Ashseal Guard
items.description: The Ashseal Warden's iron spread across a Teak Shield. A heavy guard for close fighting.

items.name: Regent Staff
items.description: Three pieces of the Furnace Regent's crown brace a Teak Staff. Casts through carried Essence.

items.name: Chainbound Sword
items.description: Living foundry chain wound through a Nightglass blade. The edge tightens under a full swing.

items.name: Nightmarshal Plate
items.description: Nightglass Plate reinforced with the bastion's old seals. Heavy overlapping ribs protect the chest.

items.name: Hollowstar Staff
items.description: Three fragments of the Hollow Star turn above a magic-wood shaft. Casts through carried Essence.

items.description: A full helm with a narrow sight slit.

items.description: Plated legs. Slower over a root field, worth it under a husk.

items.description: Plated over the toe, soft in the sole. Deepwood floor is not forgiving.

items.name: Iron Gauntlets
items.description: Fingered plate. You can hold a rod in these, badly.

items.name: Ash Wand
items.description: Dark ash with an empty crown. Its polished wood remains unlit on its own.

items.name: Ash Staff
items.description: Dark ash banded in Iron around an empty, unlit crown.

items.name: Thick Hide Hood
items.description: Deepwood hide, still faintly thorned along the seam.

items.name: Thick Hide Robe
items.description: Heavy hide, waxed. Sheds a Thornbound's spores and most of the rain.

items.name: Thick Hide Leggings
items.description: Long hide leggings cut for a full stride.

items.name: Thick Hide Boots
items.description: Laced to the knee against the root field.

items.name: Thick Hide Wraps
items.description: Wrapped to the second knuckle. Casting hand stays free.

items.name: Cobalt Dagger
items.description: A punch of black Cobalt with a needle point. It goes through moor-rot like paper.

items.name: Cobalt Sword
items.description: Hillcrest's best. Cobalt holds an edge through stone, which is the whole point up here.

items.name: Oak Shield
items.description: Oak faced in Cobalt. It rings when a bear hits it, and the bear stops.

items.name: Cobalt Helm
items.description: A closed helm with a stone-cutter's brow ridge.

items.name: Cobalt Plate
items.description: Three bars of Cobalt. Quarry crews were buried in these, which is not a selling point.

items.name: Cobalt Greaves
items.description: Full leg plate, hinged at the knee.

items.name: Cobalt Boots
items.description: Cleated for wet cairn stone.

items.name: Cobalt Gauntlets
items.description: Cobalt over the knuckle, garnet rivets. Loud.

items.name: Oak Wand
items.description: Resin-dark oak with an empty Cobalt socket and no light of its own.

items.name: Oak Staff
items.description: A two-handed oak shaft with an empty Cobalt cage. It stays dark until upgraded.

items.name: Fur Hood
items.description: Cut from a bear's winter coat. It does not take dye and it does not tear.

items.name: Fur Robe
items.description: Three pelts, stitched with Cobalt wire. Quarry Warden's floor is survivable in this.

items.name: Fur Leggings
items.description: Pelt to the ankle, weighted at the hem so it does not lift on the moor.

items.name: Fur Boots
items.description: Silent on stone. The quarry crews would have hated them.

items.name: Fur Wraps
items.description: Pelt strips to the wrist. Garnet dust worked into the weave.

items.name: Cave Ogre Sword
items.description: Cobalt worked smooth as sea glass. It swings like it remembers the water.

items.name: Cave Ogre Staff
items.description: Oak bleached and salt-cured. The cage weeps a little in the cold.

items.name: Galeskin Sword
items.description: Copper pattern, but the edge whistles on the backswing. A spare blade from Galeskin's guarded store.

items.name: Galeskin Staff
items.description: Pine scoured silver by Fallowmarch wind. The empty socket hums before a gust.

items.name: Forest Ogre Sword
items.description: A Iron blade grown through with moss that will not die. It never rusts.

items.name: Forest Ogre Staff
items.description: Ash with a living green seam. Warm at the grip like a root in summer.

items.name: Titanium Dagger

items.name: Titanium Sword
items.description: Kiln-forged and quenched twice. The edge holds a dull orange line in the dark.

items.name: Walnut Shield

items.name: Titanium Helm

items.name: Walnut Staff

items.name: Heavy Hide Wraps

equipment.name: Cobalt Sword

equipment.name: Cobalt Helm

equipment.name: Cobalt Plate

equipment.name: Cobalt Greaves
equipment.description: Full leg plate, hinged at the knee.

equipment.name: Cobalt Boots
equipment.description: Cleated for wet cairn stone.

equipment.name: Cobalt Gauntlets
equipment.description: Cobalt over the knuckle, garnet rivets. Loud.

equipment.name: Oak Wand

equipment.name: Oak Staff

equipment.name: Fur Robe

equipment.name: Fur Leggings

equipment.name: Fur Boots

equipment.name: Fur Wraps
equipment.description: Pelt strips to the wrist. Garnet dust worked into the weave.

equipment.name: Cave Ogre Staff

equipment.name: Forest Ogre Staff

presentation.description: A broad-antlered stag browses on duskoak shoots along shaded woodland margins and flees when approached.
A small russet field-runner with dark-tipped ears, bristled cheeks, and a banded brush tail. It searches the Fallowmarch hedges for seeds and beetles, fleeing from danger unless cornered.
Broad paws, tufted ears and a short tail mark this solitary clearing hunter. Its heavy paw strike has a long recovery.
A heavy red-maned minotaur with broad horns, plated shoulders and four powerful limbs. It guards the stump belt with a close horn charge.
A heavy quilled animal browsing exposed roots. Slow attacks and a tough coat reward a deliberate approach.
A muscular bay horse with a full mane, dark points and pale socks. It grazes open grass and defends itself with a forward hoof strike.
Thick fleece and curled horns distinguish this broad sheep from ibex. A slow planted ram protects its grazing shelf.
A high-shouldered marsh browser with palmate antlers and a hanging throat bell. Needs broad dry banks and room to turn.
A smooth-backed forest browser with a short flexible snout. Keeps to sheltered dry ground beside the marsh.
A long flat-jawed bank predator with a heavy tail. Basks on dry ground and answers provocation with one weighty bite.
A small-headed crawler sheltering beneath warm damp stone. Its flexible body recoils behind a quick jaw strike.
A domed shell carries this slow ledge browser. Its beak reaches out between long rests; magic gets through its armor more easily.
A raised long-necked lizard with a whip tail and spread claws. Patrols dry scree and snaps more often than the crocodile.
A long-necked broad-billed bird on the dry reed margin. Spreads its wings and pecks when provoked.
A narrow reed hunter with long legs and a spear bill. Stands between deliberate steps on a dry bank.
A tall deep-chested ground bird ranging the open shelves. Displays before closing with fast light blows.
A compact russet-and-gold field bird with a raised feather crest and sturdy running legs. It pecks for grain along the Fallowmarch field margins and darts away when threatened.
A spiral-shelled crawler on damp stone. Its eye stalks retract while the shell remains rigid.
Six planted legs brace a compact shell and branching mandibles. Its slow clamp leaves a long recovery.
Paired legs travel in a wave beneath linked armored segments. The forward jaws strike while the body remains on its ground route.
A six-legged woodland rootweaver with mottled bark armor, moss seams and hooked forelegs. It strikes with its plated mouth.
A plated insectoid biped with heavy clawed forearms. Ranges abandoned kiln courts and commits to a slow powerful strike.
A squat armored drake with dorsal plates and a heavy horned head. Holds an outer quarry bench rather than chasing far.
A tall thin-winged insectoid walking on long jointed legs. Quick raptorial claws make it dangerous in sheltered ravines.
A young pale dragon with four clawed legs, broad veined wings and limestone-colored scales.
A slender green viper with faint grass-bright markings. It stays low in meadow cover and strikes only when disturbed.
A small leaf-armored wasp with moss and amber chitin, veined petal wings and a hooked thorn stinger.
Rust and heather markings cover this small thorn-tailed wasp. Its broad petal wings carry it between dry scrub nests.
A slate-blue fantasy wasp with copper-veined wings and a curled armored abdomen, guarding reed beds with its thorn stinger.
A small armored bank scavenger. Holds its ground when attacked.
A small six-legged briar weaver with amber and ivory shell markings, jointed searching legs and a quick snapping mouth.
A compact rat with a pale line of grain dust across its back. It scavenges old stores and darts away from people.
A dark red worm nosing through the grass outside Coldbrace.
A small golden jackal with curled thorn horns, coarse fur and a dark dorsal ridge. It forages along the dusk hedges.
A small six-legged weaver with moon-silver plates, jade seams and fine woven markings.
An ice-blue shell protects this slow highland browser.
A copper crawler whose skin glows like cooling embers.
A small six-legged weaver with layered violet mineral plates and pale crystalline seams.
A broad, low stone guardian with weathered chalk plates and a deliberate hammering gait.
A leafless, petrified forest guardian. Its split trunk bends forward before a sweeping root-arm strike.
A hollow shroud drifting above the graves. Its hem and outstretched hands move without a walking step.

In woodland clearings, Bramble Tillers loosen packed soil with their hoe-shaped forearm shoots and clear growth crowding young trees. Green cambium and pale lichen mark their living bark. They push back when anyone tramples the roots they tend.
A six-legged fen scavenger with mottled swamp chitin and curved feeding blades beneath its low front shield.
A six-legged wetland mimic with a raised reed-thin body, folded walking limbs, tapered abdomen and a long split feeding mask.
A purple flower maw on a teal thorn bulb, carried by four hooked root legs. Toothed petals open around its central bite.
A small russet heath hare with tall ears, cream cheek fur and a charcoal saddle. It bounds through low cover and kicks when cornered.
A hunched stone giant with long, heavy arms. Banked heat shows through narrow cracks in its cooled ash hide.
A low mineral crawler with jointed stone legs, cooled slag plates and copper-red seams.
A votary in a pale ash cowl and scorched maroon robes. A dark face slit sits above its long reaching hands.
A crouched corpse with cold pale skin and torn dark clothing. Its long arms hang beside a lean, hunched torso as it searches the graves.
A hooded apparition in worn ceremonial cloth. Long sleeves follow its hooked hands through a sweeping strike.
A low, weathered slab creature with a recessed head and heavy hammer forearms. It transfers its weight before striking.
A six-legged burrower with charcoal flint plates, bronze mineral seams and blunt crushing mandibles.
A carved limestone sentinel with weathered stone limbs and a dark blue oath sash. It guards the sealed vault.
A pale six-legged cave weaver with a ribbed ivory shell and long searching forelegs. It feels for movement before lunging.
An eroded stone effigy with tapered stilt legs, a closed split hood and flat forearms. It turns its torso to listen across the scree.
A red hatchling with a broad brow, short tail and developing wing fingers. It braces on its rear claws before snapping forward.
A low black hatchling with a short hooked muzzle, round throat and broad small wings. It stalks the charcoal flats.
A lean volcanic dreadwing with a tucked throat, long tail and copper-red hide above an ochre underside.
A tall red wyvern with a spear-shaped skull, hooked wing claws and a long blade tail. Its rear legs brace a heavy neck strike.
A black four-legged dragon with a long low neck, backward crown horns and broad sail wings.
A narrow-bodied dreadwing with a raised throat, long legs and a swept tail. Pale horns break up its plum hide and violet wing membranes.
A lean purple dragon with a long neck and dark sail wings. Fine amethyst light follows the grain of its scales.
A massive mineral crawler with layered basalt armor and ember-lit fissures. Its heavy body settles low when slain.

worldRegions.name: Farmland
worldRegions.lore: The last surveyed land before the maps stop being useful. Two generations ago the Trade Company drove a road north, planted a bank vault at the end of it, walled a town around the vault, and then stopped answering letters. What is left is Millfield: two hundred people pulling Copper ore out of a shallow pit and pretending the wind off the northern moor does not sound like anything.

worldRegions.name: Woodlands
worldRegions.lore: Within two hundred metres of the gate the sky closes. The Ash here are old enough that the Trade Company surveyors marked them as terrain rather than trees. Oakwood is the only settlement: nine buildings and a bank chest built on and around a stump so large the stump is the town square. The people there will tell you which paths are safe. They will not tell you why the stags only move at the edges of the clearings.

locations.name: Forest Gate
locations.blurb: Woodlands's gate onto the Farm Road. Named for the direction, not the compass.

locations.name: Oakwood
locations.blurb: Nine buildings around a Ash stump the size of a square.

locations.name: Mountain Gate

locations.name: Ash Border

worldRegions.name: Highlands
worldRegions.lore: Farmland tilted sixty degrees with the soil taken away. The moor climbs in terraces of grey slate and every flat surface on it is covered in cairns nobody in Hillcrest built and nobody in Hillcrest will move. The outpost is a quarry camp with a wall, kept alive by Cobalt and by the fact that the crew stopped digging six months ago. What they hit was the Stone Cavern. They have a rota for who watches the entrance. They have never discussed sealing it.

locations.name: Highland Gate
locations.blurb: Where the Woodlands road tips over onto the first terrace.

locations.name: Moor Road Bend
locations.blurb: The quarry road forks here: down to the Lower Quarry, or up to Hillcrest.

locations.name: Lower Quarry
locations.blurb: Terrace one. Five Cobalt faces, and the hole the crew stopped digging.

locations.name: Stone Cavern

worldRegions.name: Ashlands
worldRegions.lore: The foothills north of the old survey line, where the ground runs warm and the pines grow back scorched. Somebody fired kilns here long before the Trade Company drew its maps, and the ground never entirely went out. Ashford is the camp that grew up on the warm flat in the middle: smiths, mostly, because Titanium is the first metal since Cobalt worth the walk, and the walk is why they stay. Nobody watches the southern border. There is no border. You just notice, somewhere past the last milestone, that the wind has gone warm.

npcs.name: Warden Ilse

npcs.voice: Precise and administrative. Complete sentences, no contractions, cites Trade Company regulations by number as though someone were still enforcing them. Never raises her voice; the joke is that she is entirely serious.

npcs.name: Pitmaster Dorn
npcs.role: Runs the Copper Pit, and the ledger that says what the Copper Pit contains.

npcs.name: Harrow the Smith

npcs.voice: Short declaratives. Rarely more than eight words. Uses two sentences where most people would use a paragraph, and never explains twice.

npcs.name: Ranger Syb
npcs.role: Walks the march and knows where the water is.
npcs.voice: Deadpan and outdoorsy. Describes weather and terrain in the same flat tone she uses for her own hunger. Dry, never bitter.

npcs.role: Hauls ore from the pit to the vault. Currently losing an argument to Warden Ilse.
npcs.voice: Loud, boastful, permanently mid-argument. Talks in exclamations and asks questions he answers himself. Every anecdote is about a distance and every distance is exaggerated.

npcs.name: Woodward Ansel
npcs.role: Keeps the Maple Grove. Decides which trees may be felled and which may not.
npcs.voice: Slow, reverent, superstitious about trees specifically. Long pauses written as sentence breaks. Calls trees by name and people by their job.

npcs.name: Seamer Juno
npcs.role: Oakwood's crafter. Shafts, hide, cord, and anything that has to hold under load.
npcs.voice: Brisk and teasing. Uses trade jargon and then translates it in the same breath, because she has explained this to a hundred people and enjoys it anyway.

npcs.name: Trapper Mott
npcs.role: Sets eleven traps in the deep wood. Has caught nothing in eleven days.
npcs.voice: Gloomy and self-pitying, and funny because he is completely sincere. Volunteers bad news nobody asked for. Counts his misfortunes out loud.

npcs.name: Foreman Arden
npcs.role: Foreman of the Hillcrest quarry crew. Stopped the dig six months ago and kept the camp.
npcs.voice: A manager. Everything is a cost, a distance, or a headcount. Gives instructions in the order they must be carried out and expects them back in the same order.

npcs.name: Quarrier Vess
npcs.role: Works the Cobalt faces. Does not like what the blue-black stone does in the dark.
npcs.voice: Blunt and physical, mildly superstitious. Curses in weather and stone. Says the frightening part flatly and then changes the subject herself.

npcs.name: Cairnkeeper Ode
npcs.role: Keeps the cairns on the moor. Nobody appointed her; nobody has argued.
npcs.voice: Formal and liturgical. Speaks of the cairns as duties rather than objects, and of the Stone Cavern as a room in a house she is responsible for. Never uses the word monster.

npcs.name: Watcher Hale
npcs.role: On the rota that watches Stone Cavern mouth. It is his shift more often than it should be.
npcs.voice: Quiet, frightened, and constitutionally unable to overstate anything. Describes a horror as an inconvenience. Trails off rather than finishing the worst sentence.
